checks: Real compiled endpoints copy only selected files through separate virtio-serial ports and a bounded host relay; the receiver verifies bytes and the sender verifies its receipt.
Both guests verify readonly system images, no network interface beyond loopback, no swap and no shared filesystem mount.
The receiver publishes the verified tree inside its LUKS2 volume, flushes, unmounts and closes the mapping before normal VM shutdown.
The synthetic external source disk is passed readonly and remains byte-identical after the transfer.
Disconnecting a real virtio-serial transfer leaves no partial transaction; the receiver closes its encrypted volume and powers down.
The compiled Linux relay transfers only metadata on its control channel and verifies hashes and receipts before reporting success.
Closing the control connection before approval disconnects both real VM ports; neither endpoint reports a completed copy.
SIGKILL of the destination QEMU revokes the relay through its socket-bound pidfd while the source VM remains live; the source endpoint fails and shuts down normally.
The synthetic document canary is absent from every recipient disk image after its VM exits; the source fixture intentionally retains its plaintext original.

prior_ci.reason: Only the two new transfer VM jobs failed: sender deadline included receiver boot. The explicit laboratory start gate was added in 760cf8c and has now also passed with the compiled relay under Linux/TCG. No new CI result claimed yet.

limits: No physical USB selection, manager confirmation, production controller capability issuance, close/lock hook or delivery into the chat is integrated.
The controller must choose the authorized private QEMU ports and keep the control connection private. The relay pins their real process owners, but does not authenticate a user or choose sessions.
Cancellation before the final marker prevents publication; cancellation or lost receipt after publication can leave a completed private copy. The service must reconcile it before chat delivery.
Transport revocation cannot interrupt blocked filesystem calls inside an endpoint. Supervisor escalation and orphan recovery remain open.
The VM proof uses synthetic disks, Debian ARM64 with QEMU TCG inside Docker on Mac. It does not prove x86/KVM hardware isolation.
The document canary scan covers the four recipient virtual disks only. The source fixture intentionally retains its plaintext original.
The owner-death case kills the destination VM before approval; its process exits without guest unmount. The other receiver cases flush, unmount and close LUKS normally.
The product relay requires Linux 6.5+ SO_PEERPIDFD on supported x86_64/aarch64 and fails when unavailable. The Mac relay binary refuses execution; its library remains testable.
